findings.mechanism: The change of default similarity_fct from util.cos_sim to util.pairwise_cos_sim alters the behavior of the loss computation. In CoSENTLoss.compute_loss_from_embeddings, the similarity_fct is applied as scores = self.similarity_fct(embeddings[0], embeddings[1]). With util.cos_sim, scores is a (B, B) matrix, and the subsequent scores[:, None] - scores[None, :] creates a (B, B, B) tensor, so the loss is computed over an unintended 3D tensor rather than the intended (B, B) pairwise comparison. The PR description acknowledges this but claims it is a bug fix. However, the change introduces a different defect: it changes the default behavior of the class, which may break existing users who relied on the old default, even if that default was incorrect. The class's docstring already documented pairwise_cos_sim as the intended default, so the code was inconsistent with documentation. The change makes the code match documentation, but it is a breaking change. The severity is high because it silently changes the loss objective for all users who do not pass similarity_fct explicitly, potentially leading to different training results. Trigger: any existing code that instantiates SparseCoSENTLoss(model) without specifying similarity_fct. Consequence: the loss computation changes from a 3D tensor operation to the intended 2D pairwise operation, altering the training dynamics and possibly invalidating previously trained models.
findings.trigger: Any existing user instantiating SparseCoSENTLoss without similarity_fct parameter.
findings.consequence: Silent change in loss computation from 3D tensor to 2D pairwise, altering training objective and potentially breaking existing models.
